## Learning goals

By the end of this week, you should understand:

- how Python and notebooks support the collection and analysis of web data;
- how to use the main environments in which course code can run;
- the basic programming ideas needed to work with web data; and
- the difference between a website and an API.

## Preparation before class

- Log in to [JupyterLab at jupyterlab.uvt.nl](https://jupyterlab.uvt.nl/).
- Open the course [Python Bootcamp](../../material/tutorials/pythonbootcamp/python-bootcamp.ipynb) and check that it runs.
- If you want additional Python practice, you may optionally use [Python for Everybody](https://www.py4e.com/) or [Kaggle Learn: Python](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/python). These resources are not required for the course.

## Opening lecture and Python Bootcamp

The opening lecture introduces:

- the structure of the course;
- how Python will be used for web data collection;
- notebooks, scripts, and cloud-based environments; and
- the difference between websites and APIs.

During the Python Bootcamp, you will practice:

- running Python code;
- working with variables and basic data structures;
- using conditions, loops, and functions;
- inspecting and saving data; and
- making a first connection to web scraping and APIs.

## Tutorial

- Python Bootcamp for web data

Work through the notebook in JupyterLab. The tutorial is the course's self-contained introduction to the Python needed in later tutorials.

## After the lecture

- Continue working through the Python Bootcamp at your own pace.
- Watch ["What is web scraping and what are Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)?"](https://videocollege.uvt.nl/Mediasite/Play/41afff385bd74db2af5fb8507350ea521d) (approximately 30 minutes).
- Note any Python concepts or setup problems that remain unclear.
